items.title: EPIC 0 — Human Gates
items.summary: Clear all human-only blockers for infrastructure, API access, and data access before technical delivery proceeds.
acceptance: All required external accounts and tokens exist and are stored securely.
The VPS and data-access prerequisites are confirmed.
Downstream infrastructure and automation work is unblocked.

items.title: EPIC 1 — Codebase Audit And Re-Baseline
items.summary: Re-baseline product, architecture, navigation, and planning artifacts to the new Tarteel-inspired target while preserving working foundations.
acceptance: Asset-inventory, product, architecture, and navigation docs reflect the new target.
Existing high-value foundations are explicitly preserved.
The repo now has a canonical roadmap for the new plan.

items.title: EPIC 2 — VPS Infrastructure Setup
items.summary: Stand up the target runtime on the VPS with n8n, Supabase, Whisper.cpp, and Groq-backed OpenClaw.
acceptance: Core services run on the VPS.
Health-check automation verifies the runtime regularly.
Security and network boundaries are confirmed.

items.title: EPIC 3 — Data Foundation
items.summary: Import Quranic text, reference audio metadata, and timestamp data into Supabase for the app and scoring workflows.
acceptance: Supabase contains the Quranic reference schema and imported content.
Al-Fatiha data is verified end to end.
Import scripts are idempotent and reusable.

items.title: EPIC 4 — Automation And Agent Stack Upgrade
items.summary: Migrate and upgrade the automation layer and agent runtime for the VPS target environment.
acceptance: VPS n8n has the required workflows.
GitHub and Plane automations are upgraded to the new runtime.
Agent runtime skills are versioned and aligned to the new roles.

items.title: EPIC 5 — Core App Refactor
items.summary: Refactor the app to deliver the Phase 1 Tarteel-aligned user journey end to end.
acceptance: A signed-in user can browse, listen, record, score, and review results.
The Phase 1 user journey is runnable on device.
The preserved foundations remain intact and tests stay green.

items.title: EPIC 6 — AI Core
items.summary: Replace mock analysis with the real Whisper scoring pipeline while preserving confidence-aware trust rules.
acceptance: Real audio can be scored end to end.
Confidence gating is enforced in stored and rendered results.
Validation evidence exists before stronger learner-facing claims.

items.title: EPIC 7 — Phase 2 Features
items.summary: Add memorization and progress features after the Phase 1 and AI core paths are validated.
acceptance: Memorization and progress features build on the stable Phase 1 flow.
Progress data comes from real recitation sessions.
Phase 2 remains scoped after the Phase 1 launch.

items.title: Purchase Hostinger KVM 4 VPS
items.summary: Provision the target Hostinger VPS and confirm SSH and OpenClaw access.
acceptance: The VPS is provisioned and reachable over SSH.
OpenClaw is visible and running.
Access details are stored securely outside the repo.

items.title: Create Groq free account and store API key
items.summary: Create the Groq account and secure the API key for the VPS agent runtime.
acceptance: The account exists with a working API key.
The key is stored securely and not committed to the repo.
A test request succeeds.

items.title: Generate GitHub Personal Access Token for n8n automation
items.summary: Create the GitHub token needed for webhook and PR automations.
acceptance: The token exists with the required repo scopes.
The token is stored securely.
Automation can use the token without manual re-entry.

items.title: Generate Plane API key for n8n automation
items.summary: Create the Plane token and capture the workspace and project identifiers.
acceptance: The token exists and is stored securely.
Workspace slug and project ID are recorded.
Plane automation has the required credentials.

items.title: Sign up at QUL and confirm Al-Husary data availability
items.summary: Confirm the required QUL reference data is available for the planned scoring architecture.
acceptance: QUL access is confirmed.
Al-Husary ayah audio and timestamps are verified or an alternative is reported.
The data-foundation plan can proceed with confidence.

items.title: Confirm Tarteel API is still unavailable (final check)
items.summary: Perform one final check for a public Tarteel API before the architecture proceeds without it.
acceptance: Tarteel API status is confirmed.
If an API exists, the plan is revisited before Epic 6.
If no API exists, the current architecture assumption stands.

items.title: Audit existing codebase against new Tarteel-aligned target
items.summary: Classify current assets as keep, refactor, replace, or retire against the new product direction.
acceptance: The repo has a written asset inventory.
Protected foundations are called out explicitly.
The audit is based on current code, not assumptions.

items.title: Update product vision and scope docs to Tarteel-aligned target
items.summary: Refresh the canonical product docs to match the new launch and Phase 2 direction.
acceptance: Vision and MVP scope reflect the new launch target.
Tarteel alignment is documented explicitly.
User stories match the new flow.
notes: Completed in docs/product/vision.md, docs/product/mvp-scope.md, docs/product/user-stories.md, and docs/product/tarteel-alignment.md.

items.title: Update architecture docs to reflect new infrastructure
items.summary: Refresh system and audio architecture docs for the VPS, Supabase, Whisper, and Groq runtime model.
acceptance: System overview reflects the new runtime split.
Audio pipeline reflects Supabase and asynchronous scoring.
Infrastructure boundaries are documented.
notes: Completed in docs/architecture/system-overview.md, docs/architecture/audio-pipeline.md, and docs/architecture/infrastructure.md.

items.title: Produce keep/replace decision for navigation and screen structure
items.summary: Define the target screen map for Phase 1 and Phase 2 and classify what exists today.
acceptance: The new screen hierarchy is documented.
Existing screens are classified as keep-refactor, replace, or new-build.
No premature implementation is mixed into the audit.

items.title: Add n8n to docker-compose.yml alongside OpenClaw
items.summary: Add and boot the n8n service on the VPS next to the existing OpenClaw runtime.
acceptance: n8n is accessible on the VPS.
An admin account is created.
The service is running under Docker.

items.title: Deploy Supabase self-hosted via Docker
items.summary: Deploy the self-hosted Supabase stack on the VPS and isolate it on the internal network.
acceptance: Supabase Studio is accessible.
Anon and service-role keys are captured securely.
OpenClaw cannot reach Supabase directly.

items.title: Install and test Whisper.cpp on VPS
items.summary: Install Whisper.cpp in server mode and verify Arabic transcription performance on the VPS.
acceptance: Whisper.cpp is installed and reachable over HTTP.
Arabic audio transcription succeeds.
Response time is acceptable for the planned early cohort.

items.title: Configure OpenClaw to use Groq API
items.summary: Configure OpenClaw to use Groq as its reasoning backend and verify workflow triggering.
acceptance: OpenClaw uses Groq rather than local Ollama.
Reasoning and code models are configured.
OpenClaw can trigger n8n successfully.

items.title: Build Workflow 0 — Health check
items.summary: Create the first VPS n8n workflow to verify Supabase, Whisper, and Groq health regularly.
acceptance: The workflow runs every five minutes.
Results are logged to agent operations storage.
Failures are captured without noisy human escalation on the first miss.

items.title: Create Supabase database schema for agent operations
items.summary: Create the operational tables and extensions required for agent memory and workflow logging.
acceptance: Agent memory and logging tables exist.
pgvector is enabled for future use.
The health-check workflow can write logs successfully.

items.title: Create Supabase schema for Quranic content
items.summary: Create the Supabase schema for Surahs, words, reference audio, and timestamps.
acceptance: The Quranic content tables exist with indexes.
Foreign keys are valid.
The schema supports ayah-level lookup and timing retrieval.

items.title: Download QUL data assets
items.summary: Download the required QUL JSON assets and upload reference audio to Supabase Storage.
acceptance: Required JSON data exists in the repo data folder.
Audio files are uploaded to the storage bucket rather than committed to git.
The import scripts have the source assets they need.

items.title: Write and run QUL import scripts
items.summary: Create idempotent scripts that load Surahs, words, timestamps, and audio metadata into Supabase.
acceptance: The import scripts are idempotent.
Core row counts are populated.
At least Al-Fatiha is fully usable for testing.

items.title: Verify data integrity with test queries
items.summary: Verify that imported Quranic content and reference audio metadata are correct and queryable.
acceptance: The verification queries pass for Al-Fatiha.
Timing data is ordered and complete for the tested slice.
The imported dataset is usable for Phase 1.

items.title: Migrate existing n8n workflow definitions to VPS
items.summary: Import the checked-in n8n workflows into the VPS runtime and update runtime-specific credentials and URLs.
acceptance: Checked-in workflow definitions are imported to the VPS runtime.
Runtime credentials and URLs are updated safely.
Workflows activate without import errors.

items.title: Build GitHub → Plane automation workflow
items.summary: Create a push-triggered workflow that summarizes branch activity and comments on or creates the corresponding Plane task.
acceptance: Push events are received and summarized.
The correct Plane task is commented on or created.
The workflow logs its actions.

items.title: Build GitHub PR → automated code review workflow
items.summary: Create a PR review workflow that posts Groq review comments only when CodeRabbit has not already handled the review.
acceptance: PR events trigger the workflow.
Duplicate bot reviews are avoided when CodeRabbit is already active.
Review actions are logged.

items.title: Build Plane new task → decomposition workflow
items.summary: Create a Plane-triggered decomposition workflow that expands sufficiently detailed work into child tasks.
acceptance: Well-described tasks are decomposed into subtasks.
Vague tasks are flagged for clarification instead.
All actions are logged.

items.title: Build daily standup workflow
items.summary: Create a weekday standup workflow that summarizes recent commits, open tasks, and failed agent runs.
acceptance: The workflow runs on weekday mornings Cairo time.
The summary covers completed work, in-progress work, and blockers.
The summary is posted back into the execution system.

items.title: Update and version all skills.md files for new agent roles
items.summary: Create the runtime skills set for orchestration, review, planning, connectors, error handling, standups, specs, and speech QA.
acceptance: The required skills files exist.
Each skill has version and model metadata.
The agent runtime roles are aligned to the new plan.
notes: Completed in the repo-level skills/ directory.

items.title: Configure Supabase client in app
items.summary: Add the Supabase client to the app without breaking the existing analysis-service abstraction.
acceptance: The app has a typed Supabase client entrypoint.
Environment variables are documented and wired safely.
Tests and type checks remain green.

items.title: Implement user authentication screens
items.summary: Add sign-in and sign-up flows backed by Supabase Auth and route users into the new app flow.
acceptance: Auth screens render and use the shared i18n pattern.
Users can sign up, sign in, and sign out.
Navigation respects auth state.

items.title: Build Home / Dashboard screen
items.summary: Create the authenticated landing screen with quick entry into recitation practice and recent session context.
acceptance: The home screen renders for signed-in users.
It shows an empty state or the latest session summary.
The quick-start flow opens the Surah browser.

items.title: Build Surah browser screen
items.summary: Create the searchable Surah browser backed by Supabase Quran metadata.
acceptance: All 114 Surahs are browsable.
Search works correctly.
Selecting a Surah opens the Mushaf screen.

items.title: Build Mushaf reader screen with reference audio playback
items.summary: Create the Mushaf view with ayah-level playback and word highlighting backed by reference timestamps.
acceptance: Quran text displays correctly in Arabic.
Reference audio plays per ayah.
Word highlighting and ayah recording entry points work.

items.title: Refactor recording screen for production audio capture
items.summary: Upgrade the existing recording screen from a shell into a real ayah-context capture, playback, and submission flow.
acceptance: The recording screen receives ayah context as route params.
Users can record, replay, and submit audio.
Submission triggers the scoring path and shows loading state.

items.title: Build recitation result screen
items.summary: Create the result screen with overall score, word statuses, retry, and navigation actions.
acceptance: The result screen shows overall and word-level feedback.
Low-confidence words render as uncertain rather than wrong.
Try-again and next-ayah actions work correctly.

items.title: Create Supabase schema for app user data
items.summary: Create the user profile and recitation-session tables with row-level security.
acceptance: The user and session tables exist.
RLS policies are active.
Basic insert and select behavior works for a user.

items.title: Build session history screen
items.summary: Move session history to Supabase-backed user data while preserving the repository abstraction pattern.
acceptance: History loads from Supabase rather than only local storage.
Sessions are listed per user.
Past result detail can be reopened.

items.title: End-to-end smoke test of Phase 1 user journey
items.summary: Validate the full launch journey from auth through result and history on a real device or simulator.
acceptance: The complete Phase 1 journey passes end to end.
Any failures are captured as follow-up tasks.
No crashes or unhandled errors appear during the flow.

items.title: Build Whisper transcription service on VPS
items.summary: Create the thin transcription service that exposes Whisper results to the scoring workflow.
acceptance: The service accepts audio uploads and returns text, word timings, and confidence.
Arabic transcription works for test audio.
n8n can call the service.

items.title: Build audio scoring workflow in n8n
items.summary: Create the scoring workflow that turns pending sessions into scored sessions using Whisper and reference data.
acceptance: Pending sessions trigger the workflow.
Confidence gating is enforced in stored word results.
Scored sessions are written back to Supabase with logs.

items.title: Replace mock analysis service with real Supabase polling
items.summary: Swap the fixture-backed analysis implementation for the real upload and polling flow while preserving the interface contract.
acceptance: The analysis-service interface remains unchanged.
Real audio uploads and polling work.
Mock fixtures remain available for test paths.

items.title: Validate scoring accuracy on Surah Al-Fatiha
items.summary: Run the validation cases for correct, incorrect, silent, and fast recitation before treating real scoring as ship-ready.
acceptance: All planned test cases are executed and documented.
If scores are weak, the ship posture is adjusted rather than overclaimed.
The validation report exists in repo docs.

items.title: Build hidden verses memorization mode
items.summary: Add the Phase 2 memorization mode on top of the Mushaf and scoring flow.
acceptance: The mode can hide text.
Correct recitation reveals text progressively.
Mode state resets cleanly between sessions.

items.title: Build goals and streaks system
items.summary: Add Phase 2 goal and streak features on top of authenticated recitation-session data.
acceptance: Goal and streak data is stored correctly.
The goals screen renders the current state.
Streaks update from real session activity.

items.title: Build mistake history and progress screen
items.summary: Add Phase 2 trend and mistake-history views using recitation-session results.
acceptance: The screen shows per-Surah progress trends.
Frequent mistakes are derived correctly from stored results.
The visualizations work with at least one real user dataset.
